person: Denise Holloway is a 55-year-old school office secretary who is her widowed mother Ruth's representative payee for Social Security. Ruth, 84, lives in assisted living about forty minutes away, and Denise visits twice a week. Denise keeps everything in a kitchen drawer and a folder, buys small things for her mother out of pocket, and is afraid of a mistake on a federal form. Her brother Greg lives out of state and questions her decisions, so she wants every dollar to be clean. She does not type her mother's numbers into anything she does not understand.
stated_up_front: Hi, it's Denise. I'm the payee for my mom's Social Security and I think the yearly report is due, and I want to be sure her care home bill and what I spent for her are all right. Can you tell me first what you'll need from me, and especially if it's her Social Security number or bank info?

facts.about: Who the payee is to the beneficiary
facts.truth: Denise is the adult daughter of Ruth Holloway; she is not a parent of a minor and does not live with her mother, so she has no exemption from the yearly report.
$1,684 a month, deposited to the payee checking account in Ruth's name, with Denise as payee.
Maple Court Senior Living, Care Level 2. Board and care is $3,950 a month, due on the 1st, and it already includes medication management.

facts.about: Where the monthly shortfall comes from
facts.truth: Ruth's late husband's pension of $2,420 a month goes into the same account, which covers the rest of the $3,950.
A $185 monthly medication management line appeared on the August and September invoices even though Level 2 already includes it.
September's $3,950 was already paid on September 1 from the checking account; the statement shows it.
A winter coat for $89.99 and a pack of hearing aid batteries for $14.50 bought with Denise's own card, both for her mother. The eyeglasses at $212 were already paid back in March.
A $64 restaurant lunch for Denise, her husband and Greg's family on Mother's Day visit, and about $58 of Denise's own groceries. These are not to be paid from Ruth's money.
Denise's own Brightcell phone bill of $72.40 autopaid from her mother's account in July, and she wants it put back.
Ruth's savings account at the bank is in Ruth's name, with Denise as payee. It had $6,310 at the end of last year, and this year's balance is $7,150 including $21.40 interest.

unknowns: Whether the care home will agree to take the $185 medication management charge off the August and September invoices, or whether it also affects earlier months.
What the report's categories mean, such as 'other spending' versus 'food and housing', and which of her mother's expenses go in which.
Whether Denise can be paid anything for her time or the drive to see her mother.
What the deadline for this year's payee report is and what happens if it is late.
